light.label: Medium to bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates low light, but the pink fades and growth slows

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones only; keep out of direct sun

snap: A compact Aglaonema with long, pointed leaves that are bright pink and cream, speckled and edged in dark green. It grows slowly into a neat clump and keeps its colour in ordinary room light, with no pole and no fuss. Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: Aglaonemas come from the shaded forest floors of tropical Asia, from India through Southeast Asia to southern China, which is why they cope with dim rooms. Pink Star is a cultivated hybrid, selected for its colour rather than its size. It is clumping rather than climbing: new stems rise from the base and the plant slowly thickens into a bushy mound about a foot or two tall.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Water when the top two inches of the mix have dried, and use a loose, well-draining mix. Of everything that goes wrong with an Aglaonema, cold does the most damage: below roughly 15°C the leaves curl and brown, and a draught from an air-conditioner or an open window in winter will do it in a night. Keep it warm and out of the way of vents.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: It is one of the few pink plants that holds its colour away from a window. The pink sits in the leaf itself rather than being a flush that needs strong sun, so it stays vivid in ordinary room light, and fades only gradually in a dim corner. Growth is slow, which suits a desk: it stays the size you bought for a long time.
